text:
marta: Heads-up — planning to flip on the geo-weighted routing feature for inference next Tue. Goal: prefer lowest-latency region while still honoring explicit residency flags (e.g. EU-only tenants). Wanted quick reviews from infra + legal before we schedule rollout.

cheng: quick q — if a request is residency-locked to eu and eu pool is saturated, do we currently drop to a best-effort fallback or queue?

eli: today we have two behaviors depending on tenant config: queued (up to 5s) or immediate fallback to a compatible model in another region. The new flag adds weighted preference but must never bypass residency tag.

timothy: +1 on preserving residency. For infra: what's the plan for KV-cache priming across regions when routing shifts? Warmup is the main perf risk.

marta: good call. Proposed runbook snippet (short):
1) enable flag for 5% of traffic, latency-first weighting but residency-exact still honored
2) monitor cache-miss ratio + p90 latency for eu tenants and global tenants separately
3) if eu p90 > baseline + 20% OR cache-miss spikes > 3x, rollback immediately
4) after 24h of stable metrics, ramp to 25/50/100%

cheng: can we make the 5% cohort exclude high-privacy tenants? want to avoid accidental sampling.

marta: yes — cohort selection will exclude tenants with residency=EU or privacy-level=high. We'll only test on permissive tenants.

eli: infra tasks: we need an opt-in header for clients to request "latency_preference" vs "residency_preference". suggestion: use header X-Region-Hint with small JSON: 
```
{"mode":"latency"} or {"mode":"residency","region":"eu-west1"}
```
This keeps client-side explicit.

timothy: also add metric tags: routed_region, original_region_hint, residency_blocked (bool). That helps metric-level rollback rules.

legal-sarah: confirming legal POV: as long as we never route PII/regulated workloads outside declared residency, sampling on permissive tenants is fine. We need to ensure audit logs capture region chosen + reason for fallback for 90 days.

marta: noted — infra, can audit retention be 90d for routing decisions?

infra-bot: deploybot: canary policy created: geo-weighted-routing-v1 -> 5% cohort (excludes residency=EU,privacy=high). Monitoring: route.success, route.latency.p90, cache.miss.rate. Alert: p90 > baseline*1.2 OR cache.miss.rate > 3x baseline.

eli: ops checklist for rollout:
- prewarm quantized variants in eu and us (prepull images + warm KV caches)
- run a short traffic shadow test for 10m to validate miss ratios
- set automated rollback trigger to webhook to runbook-runner

marta: final Q — does weighted-routing change model variant selection? E.g., do we prefer a quantized-compatible model in region for cost reasons even if it slightly increases latency? That could break quality expectations.

cheng: we should never prefer a lower-quality variant for tenant with fixed quality SLA. We'll add model_variant_priority list per-tenant: [exact, quantized-compatible, fallback-closest]. Default for most tenants is [exact, quantized-compatible]. But for gold-tier or quality-locked tenants we set [exact].

timothy: sounds good. I'll add config knobs and expose them in the admin UI for canary control.

marta: thanks all — will schedule engineering rollout ticket and ping on this thread with time. If anyone sees missing bits shout here. :thumbsup:

eli: FYI I'll put the short runbook in the runbooks repo and link it in the ticket.

legal-sarah: lgtm from legal, please cc compliance once audit logs are visible.

marta: ack, will do.

infra-bot: deploybot: note — if rollback occurs, runbook-runner will post FOLLOWUP and open incident stub in incidents channel.
